purpose: Project-owned human movement envelope used to check that the exercise stress poses stay inside anatomically defensible joint ranges. Ranges are generous (they bound a pose, they are not targets) and are derived from several independent references plus stated project-conservative limits. Reference-only: no third-party skeleton, coordinates, proportions, weights or animation were used.
conventions: Components as reported by scripts/audit_original_v1_joint_kinematics_blender.py: flex_deg positive = flexion (shoulder/hip/elbow: distal end forward; knee: shin backward; ankle/toe: toes up; wrist/fingers/thumb: toward the palm; neck/spine/head: forward), abd_deg positive = away from the midline (wrist: radial/thumb side; fingers: toward the thumb side; spine/neck: toward the character's left), twist_deg = right-hand rotation about the distal bone direction. Left/right are mirror images; the same range is used for both sides (sign-adjusted by the audit's side convention).

joints.basis: scapulothoracic + glenohumeral elevation can reach about 180 total; humeral rotation about the long axis up to about 90-100 each way in elevated postures
project-conservative (clavicular elevation/protraction contribute a minor, variable share of elevation)
scapular upward rotation and tilt vary through the arc (about 2:1 overall but 0.9:1 to 3.8:1 by interval); not a fixed ratio
hinge about the transepicondylar axis with a 10-20 deg carrying angle; forearm rotation about 80-95 deg each way is a separate axis
functional wrist range is modest but loaded push-up support is a near 90 deg extended wrist; radial deviation is small (about 10-20 deg)
MCP flexion about 90-100 with active extension beyond neutral
hinge, flexion about 0-80 (coupled to PIP: follows PIP motion), small hyperextension; NEVER a bend opposite to PIP flexion in a grip
project-conservative (opposition is a multi-axis saddle motion; IP behaves as a hinge; the rest thumb is already palmar-flexed, so flattening it into the palm plane reads as extension)
flexion about 120 (up to about 140 passive with a flexed knee), extension about 15-20, abduction about 40-45, rotation 30-60
flexion to 140-160 passive, 80-130 in daily/sport tasks; coupled tibial rotation of order 15 deg in deep flexion
dorsiflexion 10-20 clinical (up to about 30 in loaded squatting), plantarflexion 40-55
first MTP dorsiflexion about 57-82 and plantarflexion about 17-37 (passive range larger); loaded forefoot support uses dorsiflexion
per-segment project-conservative limits; the rib cage stiffens and distributes thoracic motion
